capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Thebes, Herakleopolis'; Osorkon III 'went on to rule Upper Egypt including Thebes for 28 years'. The Third Intermediate Period infobox gives 'Heracleopolis Magna (c. 837-728 BC, Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt)'; one dot is drawn, at Thebes. The gazetteer lacks Herakleopolis (Ihnasya el-Medina, 29.09 N 30.93 E).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -837..-801: Upper Egypt. Infobox 'Established: 837 BC', 'Capital: Thebes, Herakleopolis'; the Third Intermediate Period page: the 'Upper Egyptian Libyan Twenty-third Dynasty'. This is the shape Cliopatria assigns to the Twenty-second Dynasty row (166,128 km2, 23.4-29.3 N, Aswan to the Fayum edge). The page names no area.

correction.text: use the Cliopatria shape drawn for the Twenty-second Dynasty: Upper Egypt, Thebes to Herakleopolis; Leontopolis in the Delta is a small enclave the pages do not locate

keyframe_review.note: -800..-751, 61,633 km2 (52,603 km2 resolved), bbox 28.8-31.7 N, 29.1-32.8 E: the Delta and the Fayum edge. The page puts the dynasty at Thebes and Herakleopolis ('Capital: Thebes, Herakleopolis') and gives it 'Upper Egypt including Thebes' under Osorkon III (798-769); only Leontopolis ('Prince Pedubastis proclaimed himself king, and reigned from Leontopolis') lies in the Delta. The Delta is the Twenty-second Dynasty's: use the shape Cliopatria drew for the 22nd.

correction.text: use the Cliopatria shape drawn for the Twenty-second Dynasty for -750..-729: Upper Egypt, Thebes to Herakleopolis; Kush from 728

keyframe_review.note: -750..-701, same Delta shape, wrong the same way; the dynasty also ends in 728 on the infobox ('Disestablished: 728 BC'), though the king table runs Ini 720-715 and the page names Shabataka in 712. Use the Upper Egypt shape to 728; Kush holds it afterwards.

region.text: Upper Egypt with Thebes and Herakleopolis

ledger.note: 837: the Twenty-third Dynasty is established in Upper Egypt. Infobox 'Established: 837 BC'; the Third Intermediate Period infobox 'Heracleopolis Magna (c. 837-728 BC, Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt)'; the Third Intermediate Period page: 'found the Upper Egyptian Libyan Twenty-third Dynasty'. The page does not name the land beyond the capitals Thebes and Herakleopolis, so the region is the reading. [Reviewer me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Removed a quote about Pedubastis at Leontopolis, which belongs to the civil war of Takelot II's fifteenth year (826), not to 837 or Upper Egypt.

region.text: Thebes and Upper Egypt, the land the two lines contested

ledger.note: 826: civil war breaks out. 'In Takelot II's fifteenth year a civil war broke out' (Takelot II, 840-815 on this page: year 15 = 826). The page does not say where it was fought; Thebes and Upper Egypt, the land the two lines shared, is the reading.

799: the civil war is resolved. 'The conflict was only resolved in Year 39 of Shoshenq III' (837-798 on the 22nd Dynasty page: year 39 = 799); Osorkon III (798-769) then 'went on to rule Upper Egypt including Thebes for 28 years'.

region.text: Thebes, Herakleopolis and Upper Egypt, with Leontopolis in the Delta

ledger.note: 728: Piye of Kush takes Upper Egypt. Victory Stela 'campaigns between 728 and 716 BC'; 'Piankhy, king of Napata, put an end to the so-called Libyan anarchy' (23rd page); the Third Intermediate Period page has Piye marching north 'around 732 BC' and Iuput II of Leontopolis defeated. The infobox end 728 is used; Thebes may already have been Kushite earlier (Kashta, 8th century).

728: the Twenty-third Dynasty ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 728 BC' (the same page's table runs Ini 720-715 and names Shabataka in 712, the Payraudeau list Iuput II c. 730-710: native kings under Kushite overlordship).

wars.name: Theban civil war of Takelot II
wars.outcome: Resolved in Year 39 of Shoshenq III; Osorkon III rules Upper Egypt including Thebes 798-769.
wars.note: The location is not on the pages; Takelot II is a 23rd Dynasty king on this page and absent from the 22nd Dynasty's table.

wars.name: Piye's conquest of Egypt

zones.text: Upper Egypt from Thebes to Herakleopolis and Hermopolis

wars.outcome: Kushite victory over Peftjaubast of Herakleopolis, Nimlot of Hermopolis, Iuput II of Leontopolis, Tefnakht of Sais and Osorkon IV; the Twenty-fifth Dynasty follows.
wars.note: Third Intermediate Period page: 'around 732 BC his successor, Piye, marched north and defeated' them; Kush page: 'seized control of Lower Egypt around 727 BC'.

certainty.note: The pages describe towns and kings, not frontiers; the Thebes/Herakleopolis and Delta lines are approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt' (-800..-701, shapes -800 and -750) is a Delta shape (52,603 km2 resolved, 28.9-31.5 N) while the pages put this dynasty in Upper Egypt (Thebes, Herakleopolis); Cliopatria's 'Twenty-second Dynasty' shape (Aswan to the Fayum) is the Upper Egypt one. The two rows look swapped and both dossiers say so. The row's Seshat id eg_thebes_libyan is shared by both.
Disagreements: the infobox ends the dynasty 728 BC but its table runs to Ini (720-715) and the page names Shabataka in 712 and Payraudeau's Iuput II c. 730-710; the page's Harsiese A (880-860) and Takelot II (840-815) are 22nd Dynasty kings or Theban rivals on other lists; the 22nd Dynasty page does not list Takelot II at all. The page gives Pedubast I 829-804 while the infobox establishes the dynasty in 837. The ruler strip is omitted because the table overlaps (co-regents Iuput I, Pedubast I; Takelot III and Osorkon III).
Not on the pages opened: where the civil war was fought; the Leontopolis kingdom's land; when Thebes passed to Kush (Kashta, 8th century, no year); Shoshenq V at Herakleopolis c. 766 (an enclave of the 22nd inside the 23rd's land). A gap-filler should open 'Libyan period', 'Takelot II', 'Osorkon III', 'Kashta', 'Piye' and 'Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt'. Counterpart twenty-fourth-dynasty-of-egypt needs a dossier. Gazetteer lacks Herakleopolis Magna and Leontopolis. No infobox area on any page opened.
[Reviewer me-03-b, 2026-10-18] The 23rd Dynasty page also says 'most historians argue that they used Leontopolis as their capital' ('This is confirmed by Piankhy's stela, which locates Iuput II in Leontopolis'), a Delta seat, while reporting 'increasing consensus' that the parallel lines reigned 'mostly in parts of Upper Egypt'. The Upper Egypt reading and the swap of the 22nd/23rd Cliopatria shapes rest on the 22nd Dynasty page ('The so-called Twenty-third Dynasty was an offshoot of this dynasty perhaps based in Upper Egypt'; 'All of its kings reigned in Middle and Upper Egypt including the Western Desert Oases') and the Third Intermediate Period page ('the Upper Egyptian Libyan Twenty-third Dynasty'); the conflict is recorded here.
